The clearest structure I found is a forcing near ω ≈ 0.40 rad/s that multiplies state-dependent terms, plus velocity nonlinearities (sin v and v²). Additive forcing fits poorly (NMSE ≈ 0.1–0.3), and polynomial-only models do not get below ≈ 0.1 either. Those are the main findings to build on.

import numpy as np
def equation(t, x, v, params):
    w=params[0]
    C=np.cos(w*t); S=np.sin(w*t)
    return (params[1]+params[2]*x+params[3]*v+params[4]*np.sin(v)+params[5]*v**2+params[6]*x**2
            +(params[7]+params[8]*x+params[9]*v)*C+ (np.sin(x))*S*0 + 0*S)
